first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence indicates shorter onboarding improves completion, time-to-value, and early adoption. This directly addresses two current weaknesses without introducing the margin and customer-quality risks of promotional pricing. Verify memory_86 for durability and qualified-revenue outcomes, and memory_73 to assess whether its pricing lift persisted after discounts and attracted retained, qualified customers.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. The verified record shows completion increased 13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention rose 3%, directly addressing both current onboarding and activation declines while supporting sustainable revenue. Reject promotional pricing despite competitive pressure because its 18% qualified-revenue lift came with a 12% retention decline and failure by first renewal. Retain uncertainty about whether the historical onboarding effect will fully replicate under current conditions, so test rather than broadly roll out.
